info.name: iVenture Shared Equipment Booking API
info.description:
# iVenture Shared Equipment Booking API

Complete regression collection for the currently implemented backend: Health, Authentication, Equipment, Reservations, and the Approval workflow.

**Authentication**: this API uses a JWT stored in an HttpOnly cookie named `auth_token` -- there is no `Authorization` header anywhere in this API, and this collection does not invent one. See `postman/README.md` for exactly how multi-user cookie sessions are managed.

**Authorization / RBAC and ownership** are exercised directly against the real Equipment/Reservation/Approval endpoints throughout the collection (each such request is clearly labeled, e.g. "Employee Forbidden (Error Example)") rather than a separate synthetic folder -- the only endpoints that exist purely to demonstrate RBAC in isolation (`/​_authz-demo/*`) are explicitly test/support scaffolding in the backend, not part of the product API surface, and are intentionally not included here.

**Test data** is created through the real API wherever possible (an idempotent-per-run `runId` keeps repeated Newman runs from colliding). An Administrator account cannot be created through the API by design (docs/decisions.md, "Administrator Account Provisioning") -- see `postman/README.md` for the one-time local seeding step required before Admin-only requests will succeed.

See `postman/README.md` at the repository root for full setup instructions, known limitations, and how to run this collection with Newman.

item.name: 2. Authentication
item.description: Registration, login, current-user, and logout. Authentication is a JWT stored in an HttpOnly cookie named `auth_token` -- there is no Authorization header in this API. See postman/README.md, 'How authentication works', for how this collection manages three concurrent user sessions against Postman's single-slot cookie jar.

exec: // Runs before every request. Generates a unique runId (and the test
// identities derived from it) exactly once per Newman/collection run,
// so repeated runs never collide with a previous run's data.
if (!pm.variables.get('runId')) {

pm.expect(body).to.have.property('name');

pm.expect(body).to.have.property('role');

exec: // Select employeeAToken's session in the shared cookie jar before sending.
// Postman's cookie jar can only hold one 'auth_token' value per domain at
// a time (the app's real HttpOnly cookie name) -- this project tests
// multiple concurrent user sessions, so each request that must act as a
// specific user re-selects that user's captured token into the jar right
// before sending. See postman/README.md, 'How authentication works'.
pm.cookies.jar().set(pm.variables.get('baseUrl'), 'auth_token', pm.variables.get('employeeAToken'), function (err) {
if (err) { console.error('Failed to select employeeAToken', err); }
pm.test('Status code is 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('Response is a safe user representation', function () {
const body = pm.response.json();
pm.expect(body).to.have.property('id');
pm.expect(body).to.have.property('name');

pm.expect(body).to.have.property('createdAt');
pm.expect(body).to.not.have.property('password');
pm.expect(body).to.not.have.property('passwordHash');
// Explicitly clear any cookie left in the jar by a previous request so

pm.test('Status code is 401', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(401); });
